audit.name: Gerald Ratner Athletics Center
features_reviewed: Separate south gymnasium, narrower northeast pool hall and low west service/fitness wing
Flattened S-profile metal roofs with continuous masonry/clerestory envelope returns
East-facing sloping curtain walls, masonry end walls and sparse standing seams
Five primary masts built from three tapered tubes; 15 opposing secondary masts
Nine fore and six back stays per primary mast at three levels, with secondary bow stays
Curved brick arrival drum, rising parapet, recessed skylight, canopy and connected entry steps
audit.dimensions: Retain published dimensions where available; all remaining section levels, bays and secondary members are approximate exterior interpretations.
audit.fidelity_status: Source-compared optimized exterior: principal hall/service massing, curved roof/eave relationships, east glazing, primary/secondary support hierarchy and circular entrance corrected. Secondary dimensions and fittings remain simplified; this is not a measured or exhaustive detailed reconstruction.

references.view: As-built east arrival photograph and western aerial by Tom Rossiter; five masts and current 100-foot peak description.
Concept floor plan and elevations, used for hall/service-area zoning; checked against built photographs, not treated as as-built drawings.
Published engineering case text: three-member mast, 9 fore/6 back stays, three cable levels and opposite secondary masts. Text indexed by publisher; PDF fetch unavailable.
Published AISC award case text: three 18-inch HSS members and splayed cable support. Text indexed by publisher; PDF fetch unavailable.
Opening report; 125-foot mast statement differs from current university description.

remaining_simplifications: Local roof levels/curvature, mast locations and joints are photographic interpretations rather than construction measurements.
The existing 100-foot height choice is retained; the university opening report gives 125 feet and the source discrepancy remains unresolved.
Hidden foundations, internal sports fit-out, individual curtain-wall fittings and roof plant are omitted.

reviewed_views.comparison: Production GLB Explore view, unchanged camera; east-facing pool and gym glazing, separated low western service roof and circular arrival drum. Matched general arrangement against university built photographs.
East low-angle inspection of three pool and two gym mast groups, visible secondary masts, glazed frontage and connected curved entry.
West aerial comparison with the university western aerial: warm masonry hall ends, low west service/fitness wing, curved span profiles and western primary mast line.

audit.name: Rockefeller Memorial Chapel
features_reviewed: Single tall nave and continuous ridge
Eastern 207-foot carillon tower with physically open bell apertures and recessed louvers
Three monumental south-nave window bays per side and separate chancel lights
South great window, double-door arch, supported corner lanterns and entrance stairs
Stepped wall buttresses and mapped southeast covered passage
audit.dimensions: Retain published dimensions where available; all remaining section levels, bays and secondary members are approximate exterior interpretations.
audit.previous_review_decision: retained existing individual exterior after review
audit.fidelity_status: Source-compared exterior revision: major nave, roof, entrance and tower forms corrected. Decorative reconstruction remains simplified/provisional; this is not an exhaustive detailed-fidelity certification.

references.view: 1928 southwest aerial; roof arrangement and buttress rhythm
Built south entrance, great window and corner lanterns
Historic front elevation drawing, checked against the built photograph
Published tower height and overall dimensions

remaining_simplifications: Individual sculpted figures and heraldic details are abstracted rather than individually replicated.
Local window/member and section dimensions are photo estimates.

reviewed_views.comparison: Built south-front archive: widened paired-door portal below the great window; corner lanterns, front gable and connected steps. Individual sculptures and exact stone profiles remain simplified.
Southwest aerial archive: single high nave, west transverse projection, joined roof valleys, three principal south-nave bays and eastern tower placement.
University east/tower photograph: continuous stepped buttress supports, solid lower shaft, paired open long belfry apertures, upper short register and solid crown parapet.
Reverse-side technical inspection: roof returns and wall/support connections. This view was not used to claim measured northern-facade fidelity.
Production GLB Explore view: correct source geometry/material loading, grounded entry, ordinary selection without tint and surrounding campus context; no browser console errors.
